question.text: What will be the bull-bear spread in the final AAII Sentiment Survey of 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the percentage of bullish responses minus the percentage of bearish responses in the final AAII Sentiment Survey released during 2026.
question.fine_print: The source for this question can be found on the [AAII website](https://www.aaii.com/sentimentsurvey/sent_results).

research:
**AAII bull-bear spread: research brief for the final 2026 survey (as of 2026-11-17)**

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-17: The AAII results page lists weeks by survey-week date. The newest row is **Nov 11: bullish 30.8%, neutral 17.8%, bearish 51.4%**, so the spread is **-20.6** from the rounded figures. AAII's own write-up dated Nov 12 says **-20.7%**, probably because it uses unrounded numbers. The full history is in an .xls file (https://www.aaii.com/files/surveys/sentiment.xls), which I could not read. [AAII](https://www.aaii.com/sentimentsurvey/sent_results)
- Spreads computed from the same page (rounded figures): Nov 4 -14.3, Oct 28 -3.6, Oct 21 -8.9, Oct 14 -2.9, Oct 7 +1.3, Sep 30 -11.9, Sep 23 -15.4, Sep 16 -24.5 (bearish 53.3%), Sep 9 -1.3, Sep 2 +2.1, Aug 26 -11.5, Jul 15 +12.0, Jun 24 +8.8. [AAII](https://www.aaii.com/sentimentsurvey/sent_results)
- Which survey counts as the last one: AAII publishes on Thursdays for the week ending Wednesday. 2026-12-31 is a Thursday, so the last 2026 release would probably be on Dec 31, covering the week ending Dec 30. AAII published on the Jan 1, 2026 holiday last year, so a holiday is no obstacle. Because the question "resolves around 2026-12-31 00:00 UTC", there is some chance the Dec 24 release (week ending Dec 23) is the one used instead. [Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4536165-bullish-sentiment-inches-up-ahead-of-2026-shows-latest-aaii-survey)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. About 6 to 7 weekly readings remain (Nov 18/19 through Dec 31).
- 2026-11-12: The spread is below its 6.5% historical average for the 17th week in a row. Bearish has been above its 31.5% average for 40 weeks in a row. Neutral (17.8%) is unusually low, which means bigger swings between bull and bear are possible. [AAII](https://www.aaii.com/latest/article/568394-aaii-sentiment-survey-optimism-falters)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: The Motley Fool says AAII bearish readings rose from 27% in January to 51% in November, citing doubts about the AI boom. [Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/16/stock-market-crash-warren-buffett-says-this-is-best-move/)
- 2026-11-15: A TalkMarkets author says only 3 of their 8 technical indicators are positive and the 10-year Treasury yield is at 5.15%. [TalkMarkets](https://talkmarkets.com/article/more-cracks-in-the-markets-facade)
- 2026-11-14: The S&P 500 peaked Oct 6 and hit a low of 7,350 on Nov 5. October CPI rose 0.4%, above the 0.3% forecast, and the 10-year yield is above 5%. Markets largely price a 25bp Fed **hike** in December. Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang resigned Nov 12 and the stock fell about 13% that week. Brent is around $93 because of the Iran conflict. [Substack](https://augustcool.substack.com/p/market-mechanics-report-14-november)
- 2026-11-16: Bitcoin is around $64.5k with $2.1B of ETF outflows, a sign of broader risk-off mood. [Cryptonomist](https://cryptonomist.ch/2026/11/16/prezzo-di-bitcoin-rsi-rimbalzo-ancora-confermare-16-novembre-2026/)
- 2026-11-12: AAII's special question: 73.9% of respondents plan no portfolio changes because of the midterms. [AAII](https://www.aaii.com/latest/article/568394-aaii-sentiment-survey-optimism-falters)
- 2026-09-18: Bloomberg reported sentiment at a 16-month low (bearish 53.3%). [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-18/investor-sentiment-plunges-to-16-month-low-aaii-survey-shows)

## 4. Base rates and seasonality
- AAII's long-run averages: bullish 37.5%, bearish 31.5%, spread +6.5. [AAII](https://www.aaii.com/latest/article/568394-aaii-sentiment-survey-optimism-falters)
- How the spread moved from mid-November to the last release of the year:
  - **2025:** About -17.5 on Nov 13 (bearish 49.1%, bullish about 31.6%, inferred from the next week's changes) to **+15.0** on the Dec 31 week (42.0 bullish / 27.0 bearish). That is a rise of about 32 points. [AAII](https://www.aaii.com/latest/article/375402-aaii-sentiment-survey-neutral-sentiment-jumps), [Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4536165-bullish-sentiment-inches-up-ahead-of-2026-shows-latest-aaii-survey)
  - **2024:** About +21.5 in mid-November (Benzinga's figure; I could not tie it to a specific survey date) to **+3.6** on the Dec 26 release (37.8/34.2, worked back from the Jan 2, 2025 changes). That is a fall of about 18 points. [AAII](https://www.aaii.com/latest/article/246974-aaii-sentiment-survey-optimism-contracts), [Benzinga](https://benzinga.com/z/42025906)
  - **2023:** Ended at **+21.2** on Dec 28 (46.3/25.1). I could not find the mid-November value. [Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4660219-aaii-sentiment-survey-1900th-reporting-week-optimism-pulls-back)
  - **2022:** I could not find the figures.
- Pattern: in recent years the spread has often ended the year near or above its average, and in 2025 it swung from deeply negative to positive. The current -20.6 is lower than any of those years' year-end values. Over 6 weeks the spread has typically moved 15 to 30 points. Week-to-week changes of 6 to 12 points are common in 2026: for example, it went from +12.0 to -12.7 between Jul 15 and Jul 22, and from -24.5 to -11.9 over the two weeks after Sep 16.
- The 2026 readings since June have stayed between about -25 and +12, centered around -5. Readings at or below -20 (like now) have tended to bounce back partway within 2 to 3 weeks, as happened in September.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on the AAII spread.
- Related market: Kalshi's "CNN Fear & Greed on Dec 11, 2026" prices Extreme Fear at 0.23, Fear at 0.37, Neutral at 0.19, Greed at 0.20 and Extreme Greed at 0.06. That puts about 60% on fear readings in mid-December.
- Kalshi gives 0.11 to Michigan consumer sentiment going above 65 this year, which points to weak consumer mood.
- I found no expert forecasts of the AAII spread itself. Commentators treat the current extreme pessimism as a contrarian sign that stocks may do well later. [Substack](https://augustcool.substack.com/p/market-mechanics-report-14-november)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Weekly AAII releases on Thursdays: Nov 19, Nov 26 (Thanksgiving, so it may come out a day early), Dec 3, 10, 17, 24 and 31.
- Nvidia earnings (usually late November), and continuing fallout from the CEO's resignation.
- November jobs report (early December) and November CPI (around Dec 10).
- FOMC meeting Dec 8-9, where a possible rate hike is the main risk event.
- Swings in oil and geopolitics tied to the Iran conflict, Treasury yields above 5%, and the usual late-December "Santa rally" seasonality.

- Seasonality: late-December readings were positive in each of the last 3 years, but those were rising markets. This year is running far below them: -20.6 now, against roughly +10 to +20 in mid-November of earlier years. There isn't a strong documented seasonal pattern in the spread itself.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 6 weeks. The last 2026 release is most likely Dec 31, covering the week ending Dec 30. There is a small chance the Dec 24 release is used instead. About 6 to 7 weekly readings remain.

(b) **Latest value:** On the Nov 11 survey week (released Nov 12), bullish was 30.8% and bearish 51.4%. That gives a spread of -20.6 from the rounded figures, or -20.7 per AAII.

(c) **If nothing changed:** About -20.6.

(d) **If the trend continued:** Sentiment fell from -3.6 on Oct 28 to -14.3 on Nov 4 and -20.6 on Nov 11. Extending that straight line would push the spread into the -30s. However, readings at or below -20 have usually bounced back partway within 2 to 3 weeks, as in September (-24.5 to -11.9). A trend continuation would therefore probably mean something like -25 to -30.

(e) **Historical variation:**
- Weekly swings of 6 to 12 points are common, and the 6-week standard deviation is about 13 to 15 points.
- The 2026 range since June is about -25 to +12, centered near -5.
- Weekly persistence implies a 6-week correlation of roughly 0.3 to 0.4. Mean reversion toward the 2026 regime mean (-5) and the long-run mean (+6.5) suggests an expected value of roughly -9 to -11.
- Past year-end moves: 2025 rose about 32 points from mid-November to year end (-17.5 to +15). 2024 fell about 18 points (+21.5 to +3.6).

(f) **Experts and markets:** No market prices the AAII spread directly. Kalshi's Fear & Greed market for Dec 11 puts about 60% on Fear or Extreme Fear, which points to continued pessimism in mid-December. The macro backdrop is weak: a possible Fed hike in December, the 10-year Treasury yield above 5%, the Nvidia CEO's exit and oil at about $93. Commentators read the extreme bearishness as a contrarian signal. Late-December "Santa rally" seasonality tends to lift sentiment.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** The Fed hikes on Dec 9, CPI comes in hot again and AI stocks keep falling. The S&P 500 breaks below its Nov 5 low, and bearish readings reach 55 to 60% with bullish near 22%. The spread would land around -35 to -40.
- **High:** Inflation cools and the Fed holds, then a strong Santa rally takes the S&P back toward its October highs. As in 2025, bullish readings climb to the mid-40s and bearish falls below 28%, giving a spread of about +15 to +23.

In September, readings near -24 bounced partway, to about -12, within 2 weeks. So I do not expect a straight extrapolation.

(e) **Historical variation:**

(f) **Expert and market expectations:** There is no market on the AAII spread itself. Related signals are mixed:
- Kalshi's CNN Fear & Greed market for Dec 11 puts about 60% on Fear or Extreme Fear readings, so the bearish backdrop is expected to persist.
- The macro environment is a headwind: a Fed hike is priced for December, the 10-year yield is above 5%, and there is fallout from Nvidia's CEO resignation.
- Commentators treat the current extreme pessimism as a contrarian sign that a rebound may follow.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- *Low outcome:* The Fed hikes on Dec 9, CPI comes in hot, and an AI-led selloff plus an oil spike from the Iran conflict push the S&P into a correction of 10% or more. Bearish readings near 55-60% would put the spread around -35 to -40.
- *High outcome:* The Fed holds or sounds dovish, inflation cools, an Iran ceasefire lowers oil, and a strong Santa rally to new highs repeats 2025's swing. That would push bulls into the mid-40s and the spread to +20 to +25.

**Forecast reasoning:** I anchor on the current -20.6, apply partial mean reversion toward the 2026 regime center of about -5 plus a mild year-end bullish tilt, and keep the persistent bearish macro regime in view. That gives a median near -5.5 with a wide spread.
